newsitem.title: JAPAN: Cash JGBs lightly sold after Jan-Mar GDP release.
newsitem.headline: Cash JGBs lightly sold after Jan-Mar GDP release.

text.p: Cash yen bonds were lightly sold after the release of the larger-than-expected growth in Japan's gross domestic product (GDP) data for the January to March quarter.
Japan's gross domestic product (GDP) rose a real 1.6 percent in the January to March quarter from the previous quarter, or an annualised 6.6 percent, the Economic Planning Agency (EPA).
The yield of key 182nd 10-year JGB was at 2.420 percent at 0644 GMT, up from 2.405 percent just before the release at 3.30 p.m. (0630 GMT). Thursday's finish was at 2.430 percent.
"The rise of 6.6 percent was surprising, but the data was similar to past data and had a limited impact on JGBs," said a senior dealer at a long-term credit bank.
"I'm more worried about the slump in consumer spending in the April-June quarter in reaction to robust spending in the first quarter," he said.

Economists polled by Reuters had expected annualised real GDP for the January-March period to have grown 4.0 percent from the previous quarter, which registered a growth rate of 3.9 percent. Forecasts had ranged from 2.2 percent to 5.5 percent.
The Japanese government bond (JGB) futures market had closed before the key economic data was released at 0630 GMT.

Key September 10-year JGB futures ended firmer on concerns that the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) "tankan" survey due on June 25 may show a worsening in corporate sentiment. But resistance at 124.00 was holding, traders said.

"More people are concerned about a possible slowdown in the economic recovery if the results of the survey prove to be pretty bad. Few people believe in higher interest rates even if there is an an improvement in the survey," said a "Big Four" brokerage house dealer.
"But when the contract rose toward 124.00, the topside got heavier," the dealer said.

"A further rally may result in a fall in the coupon rate of the new 10-year JGB. I don't think the new bonds with a coupon rate of 2.4 or 2.5 percent will attract much interest from investors," he said. The last auctioned 10-year JGB to be issued on June 20 carried a coupon rate of 2.7 percent, sharply up from the record low 2.4 percent coupon for the May issue.
Activity was subdued in the afternoon before the release of the GDP data. traders said.
In the cash market, scattered buying emerged by midday.

Those who went short in futures after they opened higher were forced to buy them back by midday because light cash buying emerged at the long-end of the yield curve, traders said. The yield of the key 182nd 10-year JGB fell as low as 2.385 percent before finishing at 2.490 percent.
Traders said it may take time before the 190th 10-year JGB takes over as the benchmark from the current 182nd issue because both issues have been equally traded well recently.
Fujitsu Ltd's straight bonds, which were launched this afternoon in two tranches totalling 100 billion yen, were absorbed without a problem, traders said.
"People talked about Fujitsu's bonds not out of investor interest, but because the scandal-hit Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd is fiscal agent for the 12-year issue," one dealer said.

Dai-ichi Kangyo Securities Co Ltd lead-managed the 50 billion yen worth of 3.15 percent 12-year bond. The other 50 billion yen tranche with a seven-year maturity carried a coupon rate of 2.575 percent.
Daio Paper Corp also launched straights on Friday in two tranches totalling 20 billion yen.
-- Risa Maeda, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
